transport.executable_source: CONDITION_C_CLAUDE_BIN, else CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, else `claude` on PATH
transport.authentication: company-managed Claude Code broker: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN with a loopback ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
transport.bare_mode_rejected: --bare is the strongest isolation switch this CLI offers and is deliberately NOT used: its own help text states that under --bare 'Anthropic auth is strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper', which is exactly the separately billed path this experiment forbids.
transport.environment_construction: env -i; the child environment is built from nothing, so ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and every agent-session variable are absent by construction rather than by deletion
transport.working_directory: a fresh mktemp -d per invocation, containing no repository material
transport.home_directory: a fresh empty HOME per invocation, so no user-level CLAUDE.md, settings file or plugin is discoverable
transport.input_mechanism: SYSTEM block via --system-prompt; USER block on stdin
transport.output_mechanism: single JSON envelope on stdout; the reply is the `result` field

notes.transport_change: v1 of this config posted directly to the Anthropic Messages API. v2 runs an isolated one-shot Claude Code subprocess authenticated by the company broker. The research semantics are unchanged: the same frozen prompt, the same catalogue, the same hard-eligibility filter, the same validation gates, the same retry policy. Only the wire between the harness and the model changed.
notes.sampling_parameters_are_no_longer_contro: This is the one substantive consequence of the transport change and it is recorded rather than hidden. `claude --help` for version 2.1.258 exposes no --temperature, --top-p, --top-k, --max-tokens, --seed or --stop-sequences flag. Under v1 these were set explicitly (temperature 0, max_tokens 256); under v2 they cannot be set at all and are therefore recorded as null, meaning 'not controllable through this transport', NOT 'defaulted to something we chose'. Condition C now runs at whatever sampling policy Claude Code applies.
notes.determinism: NOT claimed, and less claimable than under v1. v1 could at least pin temperature to 0; v2 cannot pin anything. Every raw response is logged verbatim so a diverging rerun is visible rather than silently averaged away. Conditions A and B remain deterministic; C does not, and no comparison may assume otherwise.
notes.max_tokens: No longer enforceable at the transport. The envelope reports the CLI's own maxOutputTokens (64000 at freeze time), far above anything this task needs. A truncated or overlong reply is still a schema failure and is still retried once, never salvaged, so the validation behaviour that mattered is unchanged.
notes.samples_per_scenario: 1. Unchanged from v1. Self-consistency voting over k samples would be a different condition with a different failure profile, and choosing k after seeing results would be tuning.
notes.schema_retry: Exactly one retry, unchanged from v1. The retry addresses output FORMAT only and never hints at a preferred answer; its wording is frozen in the template's RETRY_NOTE block.
notes.transport_retry: A broker outage is not a model decision. It is retried up to twice and, if still failing, ABORTS THE RUN rather than being recorded as SILENCE — a transport error scored as an abstention would be a fabricated data point. Every wrapper exit code except 0 is classified as transport, never as schema.
notes.no_api_fallback: There is no fallback to api.anthropic.com and no code path that reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The wrapper refuses to run if ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is unset or points at api.anthropic.com, because in either case the broker would be bypassed. Absence is asserted structurally by condition_c_transport_test and by tools/check_condition_c_freeze.py.
notes.model_choice: claude-opus-5, unchanged from v1, and verified to be explicitly selectable through this transport: the CLI envelope reports canonicalModel 'claude-opus-5'. It was never substituted for availability or cost reasons.
